key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent design of printable scaffold microstructures and their spatial assignments to meet bone-scale mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous bone scaffolds that preserve prescribed mechanical responses under multiple physiological loads.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells using a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize unit-cell geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: All eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% error across six target moduli; human femur designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% of the constraint and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks, not fabrication tests or biological validation, so printable geometry does not establish clinical performance.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
